name: Kendall Hall
use: Originally animal sciences and the state Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory; current occupants unclear (COLSA per archives index)
architect: Frank Grad & Sons; builder Davison Construction
style: c.1970 modernist concrete frame, five stories with continuous window bands
statusNote: Floors being repurposed; current occupants unclear

renovations.what: Design services solicited to repurpose floors 3 and 4 (USNH solicitation; date not shown)

facts.text: Designed by Frank Grad & Sons and built by Davison Construction; funded partly by the NH Department of Agriculture for the Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory and by federal Higher Education Facilities Act funds; originally housed animal sciences.
Named for John C. Kendall, director of the Agricultural Experiment Station 1910–39.
Its transmission electron microscope was moved to a new imaging facility in Parsons Hall.
Kendall is not on UNH's October 2025 list of six buildings proposed for closure.

verdict: A 1970 five-storey concrete slab whose labs have largely moved out, now awaiting a new use.
notes: No licensed photo. Archives reference shows a long five-story concrete-frame slab with repetitive window panels; brutal-modern and plain. Current use is the main open question: old row says VDL left ~2015 and floors served as Spaulding swing space 2019–23; none of that was confirmed on opened pages. The repurposing solicitation page is undated (old row: 2019, ~$500k). Not on the 2025 phase-one closure list.
